knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE,

# The example

This tutorial builds a compact comparison of *Drosophila mauritiana*,
*D. simulans*, and *D. sechellia*. The displayed windows contain two conserved
flanking genes, `CG42797` and `Ptpmeg2`, with an additional `Dox` coding model
in *D. simulans*. There are 2, 3, and 2 displayed gene models, respectively.
The locus comes from [Extended Data Figure 5 of Vedanayagam et al.
(2021)](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8665063/#F11).

The example connects local gene order to exon structure, nucleotide alignment,
and transcriptional signal. It is a visualization exercise; a chromosome-wide
macrosynteny analysis would require a larger genomic window.

We will first draw three annotation panels, add two nucleotide-link panels,
and finally place a testis RNA-seq panel above each annotation. Each stage
starts with a data object and adds ordinary ggexon/ggplot2 layers. The code
uses the public object APIs and small bundled files, so downloading genomes
or remapping reads is unnecessary when following the tutorial.

# 1. Inspect the inputs

Use a ggexon version that includes `coverage_panel_height`. The complete
workflow runs on macOS or Linux because rtracklayer's BigWig backend is
unavailable on Windows. The GTF/PAF annotation and linkage steps do not require
BigWig support.

```{r dox-inputs}
library(ggexon)
library(ggplot2)

demo_dir <- system.file("extdata", "dox_synteny", package = "ggexon")
stopifnot(nzchar(demo_dir))
object_dir <- file.path(demo_dir, "objects")
windows <- read.delim(file.path(demo_dir, "windows.tsv"))
species_ids <- windows$species

knitr::kable(windows[, c("name", "accession", "chrom", "start", "end", "sample")],
  row.names = FALSE)
```

All plotting files use `X` as a chromosome-name alias. Their positions remain
coordinates on the assemblies listed above, rather than positions within a
short FASTA window. GTF starts and ends are 1-based inclusive. PAF source files
use their standard 0-based half-open coordinates; ggexon converts those starts
when importing them. Do not subtract one again after import. Supply integer
genomic bounds for object queries and stored panel windows.

The `objects/` directory contains native file views of the verified tables:

| Files | Contents | Object used below |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `Dmau.gtf`, `Dsim.gtf`, `Dsech.gtf` | Gene/transcript spans and disjoint CDS/UTR pieces | `SynIndividual`, with a feature annotation |
| `Dmau_Dsim.paf`, `Dsim_Dsech.paf` | The two sets of ungapped LASTZ blocks | `SynPairAlignment` |
| `*.RNAplus.bw`, `*.RNAminus.bw` | Forward signal and reverse-strand magnitude | `SynBigWigAnnotation` |

The GTFs are curated display models derived from the source annotations, not
new native annotations. CDS and UTR pieces do not overlap. Selecting
`annotation_type = "all"` draws both types, with thinner UTR boxes. The Dox
model contains three coding exons, with no reconstructed UTRs. CDS phase was
not reconstructed in these display GTFs.

# 2. Build the annotation data object

A `SynIndividual` holds one assembly's annotation and associated tracks.
A `SynSpecies` collects the three individuals and, later, their alignments.
`SynIndividual(annotation_file = ...)` attaches a default feature annotation;
the plotting layers query it when the figure is built.

```{r dox-annotation-objects}
comparison <- SynSpecies(name = "Dox insertion locus")
for (id in species_ids) {
  w <- windows[windows$species == id, ]
  individual <- SynIndividual(
    id = id,
    annotation_file = file.path(object_dir, paste0(id, ".gtf")),
    annotation_format = "gtf",
    metadata = list(assembly = w$accession, original_contig = w$chrom)
  )
  comparison <- add_individual(comparison, individual)
}
individual_names(comparison)

# Store three annotation rows with the exact source windows.
annotation_panels <- data.frame(PANEL = 1:3, ROW = 1:3, COL = 1L,
  track = species_ids, species = species_ids, panel_type = "annotation",
  xlim_chr = "X", xlim_min = windows$start - 1L, xlim_max = windows$end + 1L)
species_layout(comparison) <- SynLayout(panels = annotation_panels,
  free = list(x = TRUE, y = TRUE))

# Query the object to inspect its gene records.
dsim_genes <- query_features(comparison@individuals[["Dsim"]],
  chr = "X", feature_type = "gene", all = TRUE)
as.data.frame(dsim_genes)[, c("seqnames", "start", "end", "strand", "gene_name")]
```

A full genome FASTA is not needed to draw imported features. The bundled FASTAs
contain only the selected windows, so they are not passed as whole-chromosome
genomes to these constructors. The assembly and original contig remain in the
individual metadata and the source manifest.
The documented `individuals` slot provides access to an individual by its ID;
its `annotations` slot stores the named annotation objects.

## Define colors, windows, and a common style

Keep the full selected interval visible in every stage. A named list of x
limits lets each species retain its own coordinates. RNA and annotation panels
will share the corresponding genomic window later. A one-base integer display
margin keeps the half-base rectangle edges inside the panel limits; the
files still contain only the original source windows.

```{r dox-common-style}
palette <- c(
  "CG42797" = "#246589", "Ptpmeg2" = "#246589", "Dox" = "#D55E00",
  "RNA +" = "#749CB5", "RNA -" = "#67AD91",
  "85-95%" = "#E2E7ED", "95-98%" = "#A4BCD0", "98-100%" = "#497D9F"
)
window_limits <- setNames(lapply(seq_len(nrow(windows)), function(i)
  c(windows$start[i] - 1L, windows$end[i] + 1L)), species_ids)
chromosomes <- setNames(rep("X", length(species_ids)), species_ids)
annotation_limits <- setNames(rep(list(c(0.5, 2.1)), length(species_ids)), species_ids)
strip_labels <- c(Dmau = "D. mauritiana", Dsim = "D. simulans",
  Dsech = "D. sechellia", link_Dmau_Dsim = "", link_Dsim_Dsech = "")
text_size <- 9 / (72.27 / 25.4)  # ggplot2 geom text sizes use millimeters.

plot_style <- list(
  facet_genomics(vars(track), ncol = 1, scales = "free",
    strip.position = "left", labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels),
    xlim = window_limits, xlim_chr = chromosomes,
    link_panel_height = 0.5, coverage_panel_height = 0.5,
    link_axis = "none", link_strip = "blank", annotation_axis = "all"),
  scale_panel_annotation("free_y", limits = annotation_limits),
  scale_fill_manual(values = palette,
    breaks = c("RNA +", "RNA -", "85-95%", "95-98%", "98-100%"),
    labels = c("RNA-seq +", "RNA-seq - (magnitude)",
      "DNA 85-95%", "DNA 95-98%", "DNA 98-100%"), name = NULL),
  scale_colour_manual(values = palette, guide = "none"),
  scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 1, n.breaks = 4,
    labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = " Mb", accuracy = 0.01)),
  theme_ggexon_track(base_size = 9, show_x_axis = TRUE,
    show_y_axis = FALSE, show_x_grid = FALSE, show_legend = TRUE),
  theme(strip.text.y.left = element_text(angle = 0, face = "italic"),
    strip.background = element_blank(), panel.border = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom", legend.key.width = grid::unit(4, "mm"),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(0.3, "lines"),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.margin = margin(8, 12, 8, 8)),
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)
)
```

The facet sets physical row heights. Annotation rows have relative height
**1**; linkage and RNA rows each have height **0.5**. This setting changes the space allocated to a panel. The y limits
control the signal drawn within that space and are set separately.

# 3. Plot only the annotations

Build the annotation layers separately from the data object. The first layer
queries the imported transcript structures; the second adds gene names.
Both inherit their data from `ggexon(comparison)`.

```{r dox-annotation-layers}
annotation_layers <- list(
  geom_exon2(
    aes(fill = gene_name, colour = gene_name, ymin = 1,
      xmin = xmin - 0.5, xmax = xmax + 0.5),
    annotation_type = "all", exon_height = 0.48,
    compress_introns = FALSE, utr_height = 0.45, cds_height = 1,
    intron_shape = "chevron", intron_peak = 0.22, arrow_width = 80,
    linewidth = 0.1, show.legend = FALSE),
  geom_genelabel(aes(colour = gene_name, ymin = 1),
    force_flat = TRUE, exon_height = 0.48, label_offset_fraction = 1.2,
    show_link = FALSE, size = text_size, fontface = "italic", show.legend = FALSE)
)
```

The positional columns and transcript identifiers are resolved from the
annotations. `gene_name` supplies the fill and outline mappings, so Dox uses
the same orange for its exon fill, intron connectors, and direction arrow.
Thin outlines keep the short exon gaps visible. `ymin = 1` keeps the models
on a common row, and the half-base offsets make box edges span their inclusive
intervals. `geom_genelabel()` queries the gene records and adds the names.

```{r dox-annotation-only, fig.height=3.4, fig.alt="Annotation-only stage: three species with two conserved flanking genes and an orange Dox coding model in D. simulans."}
p_annotation <- ggexon(comparison) + annotation_layers + plot_style
p_annotation
```

At this stage there are three annotation panels. The blue models show the
conserved flanks; the orange model marks the additional Dox coding locus in
Dsim. UTR pieces are thin, CDS pieces are thick, and terminal arrows indicate
strand. Genomic distances are retained because intron compression is disabled.

# 4. Attach alignments and add the linkage layers

An alignment belongs to the species collection because it connects two
individuals. Attach each PAF with the same IDs used when constructing the
individuals. In these files, the upper species is the target and the lower
species is the query.

```{r dox-alignment-objects}
comparison <- add_pairwise_alignment(comparison,
  SynPairAlignment(name = "Dmau_Dsim", target_individual = "Dmau",
    query_individual = "Dsim", file = file.path(object_dir, "Dmau_Dsim.paf"),
    format = "paf"))
comparison <- add_pairwise_alignment(comparison,
  SynPairAlignment(name = "Dsim_Dsech", target_individual = "Dsim",
    query_individual = "Dsech", file = file.path(object_dir, "Dsim_Dsech.paf"),
    format = "paf"))

# Insert a link row between each neighboring pair of annotation rows.
linked_panels <- data.frame(PANEL = 1:5, ROW = 1:5, COL = 1L,
  track = c("Dmau", "link_Dmau_Dsim", "Dsim", "link_Dsim_Dsech", "Dsech"),
  panel_type = c("annotation", "link", "annotation", "link", "annotation"),
  tspecies = c(NA, "Dmau", NA, "Dsim", NA),
  qspecies = c(NA, "Dsim", NA, "Dsech", NA))
wi <- match(linked_panels$track, windows$species)
linked_panels$species <- windows$species[wi]
linked_panels$xlim_chr <- ifelse(is.na(wi), NA_character_, "X")
linked_panels$xlim_min <- windows$start[wi] - 1L
linked_panels$xlim_max <- windows$end[wi] + 1L
species_layout(comparison) <- SynLayout(panels = linked_panels,
  free = list(x = TRUE, y = TRUE))

blocks <- pairwise_alignment_data(comparison, alignment = "Dmau_Dsim")
head(blocks[, c("tchr", "tstart", "tend", "qchr", "qstart", "qend", "nmatch", "alen")])
```

These are the same 41 Dmau-Dsim blocks and 98 Dsim-Dsech blocks stored in
`links.tsv`. LASTZ generated the ungapped, chained alignments; the retained
blocks are at least 80 bp long and at least 85% identical. PAF mapQ is 255
(unknown), rather than an estimated mapping quality. No block is removed
because it overlaps Dox.

```{r dox-link-layers}
identity_breaks <- c(85, 95, 98, 100)
identity_labels <- c("85-95%", "95-98%", "98-100%")
link_layers <- list(
  geom_nuclink(alignment = "Dmau_Dsim",
    aes(fill = cut(100 * nmatch / alen, breaks = identity_breaks,
      include.lowest = TRUE, labels = identity_labels)),
    alpha = 0.55, colour = NA),
  geom_nuclink(alignment = "Dsim_Dsech",
    aes(fill = cut(100 * nmatch / alen, breaks = identity_breaks,
      include.lowest = TRUE, labels = identity_labels)),
    alpha = 0.55, colour = NA)
)
```

`alignment = ...` selects a stored alignment by name. The layer resolves its
species, chromosomes, and interval endpoints from that object. Fill encodes
`100 * nmatch / alen`, the percentage of matching bases in each ungapped block.
This is nucleotide identity, not an orthology assignment.

```{r dox-with-links, fig.height=4.6, fig.alt="Annotation and linkage stage: two nucleotide-link panels connect the three species, each at half the annotation-panel height."}
p_links <- ggexon(comparison) + annotation_layers + link_layers + plot_style
p_links
```

The updated data object now supplies alignments as well as features. We start
a new `ggexon(comparison)` and reuse the annotation layers, then add the link
layers. An earlier plot keeps the object it was created with; updating the
`comparison` variable does not retroactively add data to `p_annotation`.

The result has five panels: annotation, linkage, annotation, linkage,
annotation. Each ribbon connects real intervals on the two adjacent genomic
rulers. The link panels have no independent genomic axis. Around Dox, the
additional Dsim sequence interrupts the otherwise conserved local structure.

# 5. Attach RNA-seq tracks to the individuals

Each individual receives two named signal annotations: `RNA_plus` and
`RNA_minus`. The minus files store the magnitude of the original reverse
signal as a nonnegative score, so both strands can be drawn above zero.
The signed audit values remain in `coverage.tsv.gz`.

```{r dox-rna-objects, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows"}
for (id in species_ids) {
  individual <- comparison@individuals[[id]]
  signal_unit <- if (id == "Dsim") "primary read depth" else "deposited signal"
  individual <- add_annotation(individual,
    SynBigWigAnnotation(name = "RNA_plus",
      bigwig_file = file.path(object_dir, paste0(id, ".RNAplus.bw")),
      metadata = list(transcript_strand = "+", signal_unit = signal_unit)))
  individual <- add_annotation(individual,
    SynBigWigAnnotation(name = "RNA_minus",
      bigwig_file = file.path(object_dir, paste0(id, ".RNAminus.bw")),
      metadata = list(transcript_strand = "-", signal_unit = signal_unit,
        score_handling = "reverse-strand magnitude")))
  comparison <- add_individual(comparison, individual)
}
names(comparison@individuals[["Dsim"]]@annotations)
```

The files contain local testis RNA-seq from biological replicate 1. Dmau and
Dsech retain deposited signal values. Dsim uses unnormalized primary read depth
from the complete original library remapped to the plotted assembly. These
units differ between the middle and outer species; the figure compares signal
shape and genomic position rather than expression abundance between species.

## Set y limits from the data objects

Query each strand over the exact selected window, then find the larger peak.
A y maximum of `1.1 * peak` puts each species' highest peak at approximately
91% of its RNA panel height. This changes the view without changing the stored
scores, smoothing the signal, or clipping its maximum.

```{r dox-rna-limits, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows"}
peaks <- setNames(vapply(species_ids, function(id) {
  individual <- comparison@individuals[[id]]
  w <- windows[windows$species == id, ]
  max(vapply(c("RNA_plus", "RNA_minus"), function(name) {
    signal <- query_signal(get_annotation(individual, name), "X", w$start, w$end)
    max(S4Vectors::mcols(signal)$score)
  }, numeric(1)))
}, numeric(1)), species_ids)
rna_limits <- lapply(peaks, function(peak) c(0, 1.1 * peak))
knitr::kable(data.frame(species = species_ids, peak = unname(peaks),
  unit = c("deposited signal", "primary read depth", "deposited signal")),
  row.names = FALSE)
```

## Store the interleaved panel order

Use an explicit `SynLayout` to put each RNA panel immediately above its own
annotation. Coverage and annotation have the same public `track` name, with
`panel_type` distinguishing their roles. The two linkage rows name their
source species. Their endpoints will continue to use annotation panels.

```{r dox-rna-layout, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows"}
panels <- data.frame(
  PANEL = 1:8, ROW = 1:8, COL = 1L,
  track = c("Dmau", "Dmau", "link_Dmau_Dsim", "Dsim", "Dsim",
    "link_Dsim_Dsech", "Dsech", "Dsech"),
  panel_type = c("coverage", "annotation", "link", "coverage", "annotation",
    "link", "coverage", "annotation"),
  tspecies = c(NA, NA, "Dmau", NA, NA, "Dsim", NA, NA),
  qspecies = c(NA, NA, "Dsim", NA, NA, "Dsech", NA, NA)
)
wi <- match(panels$track, windows$species)
panels$species <- windows$species[wi]
panels$xlim_chr <- ifelse(is.na(wi), NA_character_, "X")
panels$xlim_min <- windows$start[wi] - 1L
panels$xlim_max <- windows$end[wi] + 1L
species_layout(comparison) <- SynLayout(panels = panels,
  free = list(x = TRUE, y = TRUE))
panels[, c("ROW", "track", "panel_type")]
```

## Add the coverage layers

Select the attached signal by its annotation name. Because the two coverage
layers request the same species and windows, their forward and reverse signals
share each species' coverage panel. The species' annotation panel remains a
separate panel with its own y range.

```{r dox-rna-layers, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows"}
rna_layers <- list(
  geom_coverage(aes(fill = "RNA +"), annotation = "RNA_plus", alpha = 0.85),
  geom_coverage(aes(fill = "RNA -"), annotation = "RNA_minus", alpha = 0.85)
)
p_rna <- ggexon(comparison) +
  annotation_layers +
  link_layers +
  rna_layers +
  plot_style +
  scale_panel_coverage("free_y", limits = rna_limits)
```

```{r dox-with-rna, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows", fig.alt="Complete eight-panel figure: testis RNA-seq above each species annotation, two smaller nucleotide-link panels, and orange Dox coding exons in D. simulans."}
p_rna
```

The complete figure has three RNA panels, three annotation panels, and two
linkage panels. Blue RNA signal is the forward strand; green is the reverse
strand's magnitude. RNA peaks occupy similar fractions of their panels because
the y scales are independent. The separate units and the values in the table
above are needed when interpreting those peaks.

# 6. Adjust panel heights or compress genomic gaps

To make the linkage or RNA rows smaller, replace the facet with different
physical heights. Reuse the other facet settings so the genomic windows and
strip labels remain the same.

```{r dox-height-controls, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
p_rna + facet_genomics(vars(track), ncol = 1, scales = "free",
  strip.position = "left", labeller = as_labeller(strip_labels),
  xlim = window_limits, xlim_chr = chromosomes,
  link_panel_height = 0.3, coverage_panel_height = 0.4,
  link_axis = "none", link_strip = "blank", annotation_axis = "all")
```

A number is a height relative to an annotation row. A grid unit such as
`grid::unit(8, "mm")` sets an absolute height instead. `coverage_panel_height`
controls panel size; `scale_panel_coverage()` controls its y range. Changing
one does not require changing the other.

The following scale compresses non-exonic gaps three-fold while retaining
exon widths. It applies the same piecewise map to gene models, RNA intervals,
and both ends of every link. Tick labels remain original genomic coordinates.

```{r dox-compressed, eval=.Platform$OS.type != "windows", fig.alt="The complete object-based figure with gaps compressed three-fold; RNA signals and nucleotide links remain aligned with exon models."}
p_compressed <- p_rna + scale_x_ggexon_genomic(intron_factor = 3,
  n.breaks = 4,
  labels = scales::label_number(scale = 1e-6, suffix = " Mb", accuracy = 0.01))
p_compressed
```

Gaps include intergenic sequence as well as introns. The compressed view has
no single uniform base-pair scale. Keep genomic coordinates in the objects;
do not compress annotation, signal, or alignment coordinates before plotting.

# 7. Export the plots

Keep `p_annotation`, `p_links`, and `p_rna` as separate objects so you can
export each stage or reuse it in a presentation. These commands write to your
chosen working directory, not into the installed package.

```{r dox-export, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}
ggsave("dox-annotation.pdf", p_annotation, width = 9.5, height = 3.4,
  units = "in", device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white")
ggsave("dox-with-links.pdf", p_links, width = 9.5, height = 4.6,
  units = "in", device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white")
ggsave("dox-with-rna.pdf", p_rna, width = 9.5, height = 6.5,
  units = "in", device = grDevices::cairo_pdf, bg = "white")
ggsave("dox-with-rna.png", p_rna, width = 9.5, height = 6.5,
  units = "in", dpi = 300, bg = "white")
```

# Data provenance and interpretation

The flanks are common *D. melanogaster* RefSeq models `NM_132346` and
`NM_132348` mapped by UCSC GenArk to the selected species assemblies. The
orange model comes from the published 474-nt Dox CDS. A unique, end-to-end,
100%-identity splice alignment places it at Dsim X:9,250,280-9,250,879 on the
minus strand, with CIGAR `285M63N42M63N147M`. Joining those three coding exons
and reverse-complementing them reconstructs the published CDS exactly.
The figure does not reconstruct the full Dox transcript.

RNA-seq comes from [GSE185361](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE185361),
specifically [GSM5611558](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM5611558),
[GSM7039340](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM7039340), and
[GSM5611560](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSM5611560).
The deposited Dsim BigWigs use an X chromosome of 22,976,950 bp, whereas the
plotted GenBank assembly has 23,123,156 bp. They were excluded. The complete
original library [SRR23418969](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/ena/browser/view/SRR23418969),
containing 40,381,684 read pairs, was remapped directly to GCA_004382185.1
with minimap2's `splice:sr` preset. No coordinate offset was inferred.

Dsim coverage retains primary alignments with MAPQ >=20 and excludes intron
and deletion bases; overlapping mates each contribute to read depth.
Canonical splice motifs support a reverse-stranded paired library, with read 1
antisense and read 2 sense. Input checksums, the full reference sequence, the
BAM chromosome dictionary, and the complete-library read count were verified.
The coverage agrees with an independent samtools depth calculation at all
43,781 plotted bases. `Dsim-remapping-qc.json` records these checks and the
mapping statistics. Dmau and Dsech retain author-deposited coverage values.

`manifest.json` records original source URLs, sequence and data checksums,
BigWig extraction ranges, and alignment settings. `objects/manifest.json`
records how the native tutorial files relate to the verified tables, with
input/output checksums. The GTF/PAF/BigWig conversion changes file formats,
not the underlying genomic intervals or signal magnitudes.

For source details, see the [primary locus paper](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41559-021-01592-z),
its [Supplementary Table 1](https://media.springernature.com/original/springer-static/esm/art%3A10.1038%2Fs41559-021-01592-z/MediaObjects/41559_2021_1592_MOESM2_ESM.xlsx),
the [assembly paper](https://doi.org/10.1101/gr.263442.120), and the
[minimap2 short RNA-seq documentation](https://github.com/lh3/minimap2#map-short-rna-seq-reads).

To prepare the files again from the repository, run
`remap-dsim-rnaseq.py`, `build-dox-data.py`, then
`Rscript data-raw/dox_synteny/prepare-dox-objects.R`.
The large raw-read/reference/BAM cache stays outside the bundled inputs.
Rendering this article uses only the bundled files.
